'''Alejandro''' "'''Álex'''" '''Abrines Redondo''' (born 1 August 1993) is a Spanish former professional [[basketball]] player. He spent most of his career playing for [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]], acting as [[captain (sports)|team captain]] for several seasons. Standing at 6 ft 6 in (1.98 m), he mainly played the [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions. Abrines has won three [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] championships with FC Barcelona in [[2013–14 ACB season|2014]], [[2020–21 ACB season|2021]] and [[2022–23 ACB season|2023]]. He was selected for the [[EuroLeague Rising Star Award]] in 2016.

Born in [[Palma de Mallorca]], Spain, Abrines began his career with [[CB Axarquía]] in 2010, playing professionally till 2025. He joined [[Baloncesto Málaga]] in 2011 and was loaned back to Axarquía in the 2011–12 season. Abrines moved to FC Barcelona in 2012. He declared for the [[2013 NBA draft]] and was selected 32nd overall by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. After three more seasons with FC Barcelona, Abrines joined the Thunder in 2016 and played three seasons with the team. He returned to FC Barcelona in 2019.

Abrines has represented Spain internationally since his junior years. Abrines won a bronze medal with [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain]] at the [[2016 Summer Olympics]].

==Professional career==
===Spain (2010–2016)===
Between 2010 and 2012, Abrines played for [[CB Axarquía|Clínicas Rincón]] and [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja]]. He was traded to Spanish club [[FC Barcelona Basquet|FC Barcelona]] in July 2012.<ref>[http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=86205 Barça Regal y Unicaja acuerdan el intercambio entre Fran Vázquez y Abrines {{in lang|es}}.]</ref>

On 27 June 2013, Abrines was selected by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] with the 32nd overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2013/6/27/4470594/nba-draft-2013-oklahoma-city-thunder-alex-abrines/in/4235723 |title=NBA Draft 2013: Oklahoma City Thunder select Alex Abrines with No. 32 pick |work=[[SB Nation]] |date=27 June 2013 |access-date=27 June 2013}}</ref>

On 19 May 2015, Abrines re-signed with Barcelona until 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cauchi |first=O. |date=2015-05-19 |title=Barcelona re-signs Alex Abrines until 2019 |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/161438/barcelona-re-signs-alex-abrines-until-2019.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170820161703/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/161438/barcelona-re-signs-alex-abrines-until-2019.html |archive-date=2017-08-20 |access-date=2025-08-06 |work=Sportando |language=en}}</ref> In May 2016, he was named the [[EuroLeague Rising Star]]. He played four seasons for Barcelona, winning three titles with the club – one Spanish ACB league championship, one [[Spanish Basketball King's Cup|Spanish King's Cup]], and one [[Spanish Basketball Supercup|Spanish Supercup]]. On 19 July 2016, Abrines parted ways with Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/sections/basketball/first-team/news/2016-2017/abrines-says-farewell-to-fc-barcelona-lassa |title=Abrines says farewell to FC Barcelona Lassa |publisher=fcbarcelona.com |date=19 July 2016 |access-date=19 July 2016}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2016–2019)===
[[File:Alex Abrines (Thunder at Wizards 2-13-17) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Abrines in 2017|left]]
On 23 July 2016, Abrines signed a three-year, $18 million contract with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-abrines-160723 |title=Thunder Signs Alex Abrines |work=NBA.com |date=23 July 2016 |access-date=23 July 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the Thunder in their season opener on 26 October, scoring three points off the bench in a 103–97 victory over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899389 |title=Thunder vs. 76ers – Box Score |work=ESPN.com |date=26 October 2016 |access-date=27 October 2016}}</ref> On 21 December, he hit five three-pointers and finished with a career-best 18 points in a 121–110 victory over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899875 |title=Westbrook scores 42, Thunder beats Pelicans 121-110 |work=ESPN.com |date=21 December 2016 |access-date=22 December 2016}}</ref> On 24 February 2017, in his first career start, Abrines set a new career high with 19 points in a 110–93 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900267 |title=Westbrook's triple-double leads Thunder past Lakers, 110-93 |work=ESPN.com |date=24 February 2017 |access-date=25 February 2017}}</ref>

On 9 December 2017, Abrines, starting in place of the injured [[Paul George]], scored a career-high 20 points in a narrow 102–101 overtime victory over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975133 |title=Westbrook's triple-double leads Thunder past Grizzlies in OT |work=ESPN.com |date=9 December 2017 |access-date=10 December 2017}}</ref>

On 1 November 2018, Abrines had 25 points on five three-pointers in a 111–107 victory over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070792 |title=Thunder rally from 19 down in 3rd, top Hornets 111-107 |work=ESPN.com |date=1 November 2018 |access-date=1 November 2018}}</ref> Later that month on 30 November, he scored 21 points off a career-high seven three-pointers in a 124–109 victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/recap-hawks-181130 |title=Three-Point Barrage, 2nd Quarter Burst Fuel Thunder Win– OKC 124, ATL 109 |last=Gallo |first=Nick |date=30 November 2018 |website=Oklahoma City Thunder |language=en |access-date=8 July 2019}}</ref>

On 9 February 2019, Abrines was waived by the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/abrines-190209 |title=Thunder Waives Alex Abrines |work=NBA.com |date=9 February 2019 |access-date=9 February 2019}}</ref> After sitting out a number of games, he and the team mutually decided to part ways, citing personal reasons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Royce |date=9 February 2019 |title=Thunder release Abrines, cite personal issue |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/25960564 |access-date=2024-03-27 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Return to Spain (2019–2025)===
On 12 July 2019, Abrines signed a two-year deal with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] with the option of a third year.<ref>{{cite news |title=Agreement to sign Álex Abrines until 2021 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/1276252/agreement-to-sign-alex-abrines-until-2021 |access-date=13 July 2019 |work=www.fcbarcelona.com |date=12 July 2019}}</ref> On 30 June 2021, he extended his contract with the team until 2026.<ref>{{cite news |title=Alex Abrines signs multi-year contract extension with Barcelona |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/alex-abrines-signs-multi-year-contract-extension-with-barcelona/ |website=Sportando |access-date=30 June 2021 |date=30 June 2021 |last=Carchia |first=Emiliano}}</ref> Abrines suffered a knee injury a few months later on 17 September and was ruled out for four months.<ref>{{cite web |title=Álex Abrines undergoes knee surgery |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/2256656/alex-abrines-undergoes-knee-surgery |date=16 September 2021 |website=fcbarcelona.com |access-date=17 September 2021}}</ref> On 22 July 2025, Abrines announced his retirement from professional basketball on social media. He played ten seasons in total for the Catalans, appearing in 660 games and winning 15 titles.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alex Abrines announces his retirement from basketball |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/4319688/alex-abrines-announces-his-retirement-from-basketball |date=22 July 2025 |website=fcbarcelona.com |access-date=22 July 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Abrines has played with the junior national teams of Spain. He won the gold medal at the [[2011 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], where Abrines was named to the All-Tournament Team, as well as being named the tournament's MVP.<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.season_2011.compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.coid_5LMCE,D7HrUtCBHTVzvib3.articleMode_on.html FIBAEurope.com Abrines Named U18 MVP.]</ref> He also played at the [[2012 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], winning the bronze medal. In 2016, Abrines won a bronze medal at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Rio Olympics]] with the senior [[Spain national basketball team]]. He also played at [[EuroBasket 2017]].
